title: Dweep Tulika Public Opinion Survey 2026: 100 Voices from the Islands Reveal Jobs, Healthcare and Basic Services as Top Concerns
author: Dweep Tulika
html:
Sri Vijaya Puram | August 21, 2026

Employment, healthcare, electricity, roads and government responsiveness have emerged as some of the strongest concerns among respondents in the Dweep Tulika Public Opinion Survey 2026, conducted to understand public perceptions of quality of life, public services, governance and development in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

The survey received 100 responses between July 9 and August 20, 2026 through an online questionnaire and two days of in-person public response collection at high-footfall locations in Sri Vijayapuram, including Mazhar Pahad opposite Nescafé, Flag Point, Marina Park and Junglighat.

Employment emerges as the biggest concern

Employment and jobs emerged as the most frequently mentioned concern, appearing in 67 responses to the question on the biggest problems facing the Islands.

Healthcare was mentioned in 47 responses, followed by roads at 46, transport and public transport at 41, drug abuse/addiction at 41, youth opportunities at 38 and education at 34.

When respondents were separately asked what should be the Government's highest priority, employment again ranked first at 35%, followed by healthcare at 18%, infrastructure at 11% and education at 10%.

Electricity, roads and government hospitals receive lowest ratings

The survey asked respondents to rate public services on a scale of 1 to 5.

Electricity received the lowest average rating at 1.84/5, followed by roads at 1.96/5 and government hospitals at 2.11/5.

Ferry services received 2.41, public transport 2.46, law and order 2.48, government schools 2.56, cleanliness 2.56, drinking water 2.64 and internet connectivity 2.73.

The survey found that 78% of respondents rated electricity at 1 or 2, while 70% gave the same low rating to roads and 64% to government hospitals.

Healthcare repeatedly emerges as a concern

Healthcare appeared across several sections of the survey.

It was the second-most frequently mentioned major problem, the second-most selected Government priority at 18%, and the area most frequently identified as requiring improvement, with 27% of respondents selecting health.

Government hospitals also received a relatively low average score of 2.11/5.

Concerns over grievance redressal

Respondents also expressed dissatisfaction with how effectively government departments respond to public grievances.

The average rating for grievance redressal was 2.05/5. A total of 68% rated the response at either 1 or 2, while only 5% gave it a rating of 4 and none selected 5.

Assessment of elected representative

The survey also asked respondents to rate the performance of their elected representative.

The average rating was 2.02/5, with 42% giving a rating of 1 and 26% giving a rating of 2. Overall, 68% selected either 1 or 2, while only 10% gave a rating of 4 or 5.

On accessibility, only 18% said their elected representative was accessible “Always” or “Often”, while 82% selected “Sometimes”, “Rarely” or “Never.”

Not everyone views life in the Islands negatively

Despite concerns over specific services and governance, the survey does not indicate uniform dissatisfaction with overall quality of life.

Respondents gave an average quality-of-life rating of 3.12 out of 5. While 27% gave a rating of 1 or 2, 36% gave a positive rating of 4 or 5 and 37% selected the middle rating of 3.

When asked whether the Islands were moving in the right direction, 20% said yes, 46% said no and 34% were unsure.

A predominantly young respondent base

The survey had a predominantly young respondent group. 75% were between 18 and 34 years old, while students accounted for approximately 45% of respondents.

The sample was also concentrated geographically, with 86% of respondents from South Andaman, 13% from North & Middle Andaman and 1% from Nicobar.

What do the 100 responses indicate?

Across different questions, five broad themes repeatedly emerged:
  • Employment and jobs
  • Healthcare
  • Electricity and roads
  • Education and youth opportunities
  • Grievance redressal and government responsiveness
The survey therefore presents a picture of respondents seeking greater economic opportunities, stronger essential services and more responsive public institutions.

Important note on the survey

The Dweep Tulika Public Opinion Survey used a voluntary, non-probability sample of 100 respondents. The sample has a significant concentration of younger respondents and South Andaman residents.

Therefore, the findings should be understood as indicative of the views expressed by the participants and not as statistically representative of the entire population of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. No statistical margin of error is presented.

Dweep Tulika's takeaway

The 100 responses point towards a public looking for jobs, better essential services, stronger healthcare and institutions that listen and respond.

At the same time, the mixed quality-of-life responses show that public sentiment cannot be reduced to a single negative verdict.

This survey is therefore intended as a snapshot of public concerns and expectations and a starting point for wider discussion about the future of the Islands.

Dweep Tulika | A Truthful & Unbiased Perspective
